A multinational corporation reports its income-tax information each year. For every fiscal year it discloses:

• The effective tax rate actually incurred for several operating segments, such as "international", "domestic", "overall", etc.
• Additional one-off tax adjustments (e.g., share-based-compensation benefits, U.S. tax-reform impacts, losses on disposition) that can affect—but are separate from—the headline rates.
The public note explains that the benefit to the company’s effective income-tax rate for international operations relates to lower-taxed global activities and other funding structures. • list_segments() → list[str]
  Return all operating-segment names that have effective-tax-rate data.
• get_segment_id(segment_name: str) → int
  Translate a segment name to its internal numeric ID.
• get_effective_tax_rate(year: int, segment_name: str) → float
  Fetch the effective tax rate (percentage) for a given fiscal year and operating segment.
• list_jurisdictions_for_year(year: int) → list[str]
  Return all jurisdictions that have statutory-rate data recorded for the specified year.
• get_statutory_tax_rate(year: int, jurisdiction: str) → float
  Retrieve the statutory tax rate (percentage) for a particular jurisdiction and year.

  Convenience wrapper that returns the statutory tax rate recorded for the "global" jurisdiction in a given year.
• list_tax_adjustments(year: int) → list[tuple[str,float]]
  Get descriptions and values of one-off tax adjustments recorded for the year.
• get_effective_tax_rate_overall(year: int) → float | None
  Return the company-wide overall effective tax rate for the year if it exists.

Question to answer
What is the difference between the statutory tax rate and the effective tax rate for international operations in 2018?

Work out the answer step-by-step. Call tools whenever you need concrete figures. Show only the final numerical answer (with a % sign) in your final response.
